own-vm.note: Every Instance is a full virtual machine with its own kernel, so Docker, kernel modules and any TCP service behave as on a physical server. The hypervisor is not named in the docs.

source.quote: An Instance is a virtual machine in the cloud. Like a physical machine, it provides resources such as virtualized CPU, RAM, and storage.

root.note: You connect as root with the SSH key you upload at creation; there is also a browser serial console and a rescue/boot-mode path if the install breaks.

source.quote: you can use a terminal application on your local computer to remotely connect to your Instance as root.

docker-inside.note: Docker is a one-click InstantApp, and root means any container runtime can be installed instead.

source.quote: Docker, the famous container manager encapsulated in a Scaleway image, allows you to deploy your applications within seconds, eliminating concerns about compatibility and dependencies.

nested-virt.note: No Scaleway page states whether nested virtualisation works inside an Instance, and the datasheet lists CPU, RAM and storage without a virtualisation flag. Treat it as unavailable until support confirms; QEMU/KVM or an Android emulator inside an Instance is not a documented use case.

source.quote: This datasheet provides a concise overview of the performance, technical features, components, materials, and associated documentation for different Instance offers.

custom-image.note: Snapshots can be exported to and imported from Object Storage as QCOW2 files, so a VM built elsewhere can be brought in and an Instance can be moved between Availability Zones. You can also snapshot a configured Instance and boot copies from it.

source.quote: The snapshot transfer feature allows you to export or import Instances snapshots.

any-size.note: CPU and RAM come only in the published offer sizes; the console's resize flow picks from a list of offers rather than letting you set vCPU and RAM independently. Disk is the flexible dimension, through block volumes.

source.quote: Select a new Instance configuration from the list of available offers.

big-machines.note: Within the shared and development ranges the largest is GP1-XL at 48 vCPU / 256 GiB; dedicated STANDARD3 and POP2 reach 64 vCPU / 256 GiB, and 96 vCPU on COMPUTE3. They are outside this card but orderable on the same platform.

source.quote: vCPUs 48 vCPU type Shared RAM size 256 GiB

live-resize.shortfall: Resizing is a change of offer that reboots the Instance with up to five minutes of downtime, and it needs block storage rather than a local volume.
live-resize.note: You can move up or down the offer list, including to a newer generation, without recreating the machine. The disk cannot shrink and the machine reboots, so it is not a live resize.

source.quote: This upgrades your Instance, which reboots in the process, resulting in up to five minutes of downtime.

gpu.note: GPU Instances are sold from the same console and API, from an L4 at €0.79/hour to eight B300-SXM. They are outside this general-purpose card and cost many times more.

source.quote: A flexible, cost-effective GPU instance designed for AI and accelerated workloads

choose-region.note: Four EU regions, each with three Availability Zones; not every offer is available in every zone, and the pricing page's zone selector is the authoritative list.

source.quote: Scaleway offers different Instance ranges in all regions: Paris (France), Amsterdam (Netherlands), and Warsaw (Poland).

eu-region.note: All four regions are in the EU, operated by a French company that markets itself as free of US CLOUD Act exposure. EU location is not by itself a residency guarantee: the customer still chooses the zone and configures backups.

source.quote: A subsidiary of the iliad Group, Scaleway currently operates in France, Poland, Italy, and the Netherlands, with upcoming deployments in Sweden and Germany.

pause-memory.note: Standby mode keeps the Instance allocated and its data on local storage, but Scaleway bills it in full while it sits there, so it is not a cheaper pause. Powering off is the only way to stop the compute meter, and that loses RAM and running processes.

source.quote: You are still billed for an Instance in standby mode, as well as for its storage and any flexible IPs attached to it.

warm-pool.shortfall: An autoscaling group can hold a fixed number of identical Instances behind a load balancer, but there is no way to claim one of them for a single task.
warm-pool.note: Groups can run at a fixed size or scale on CPU/RAM metrics, and autohealing replaces failed Instances. That is a pool of running servers for a service, not a warm pool that hands a machine to a job.

source.quote: A group can run at a fixed size for predictable workloads, or scale automatically between a minimum and maximum number of Instances based on usage metrics.

fast-start.note: Scaleway says its Instances are delivered in seconds. Provisioning includes cloning the image onto a volume and booting a kernel, so this is not a sub-second sandbox start.

source.quote: Our Virtual Instances range is delivered in seconds and is made to meet all your workload needs, from personal projects to business-critical apps.

snapshot-files.note: A snapshot copies one volume, and an image snapshots every volume of an Instance. Snapshots are independent billed resources kept until deleted, and can be exported as QCOW2.

source.quote: Creating an image makes a complete backup of your Instance, including all of its volumes.

snapshot-memory.note: A snapshot is a picture of a volume, not of RAM. Restoring one boots a fresh kernel, and anything the agent held in memory is gone.

source.quote: A snapshot takes a picture of a specific volume at one point in time.

fork-running.note: There is no copy-on-write fork of a running machine. The closest is a crash-consistent snapshot of a running volume followed by creating a new Instance from it.

source.quote: A snapshot takes a picture of a specific volume at one point in time.

older-snapshot.note: Snapshots are not rotated automatically and survive the deletion of their source volume, Instance or image, so any age is available until you delete it.

source.quote: In both cases, the snapshot exists as an independent, billed resource and is not deleted when its source volume, Instance, or image is deleted.

templates.note: A template stores the offer, image, network, security group, tags and cloud-init for repeatable creation. It cannot be edited after creation; you create a new one or override fields at deploy time.

source.quote: An Instance template saves a predefined, immutable server configuration

backups.note: There is no automatic backup product for Instances: images and snapshots are manual, and Scaleway documents a do-it-yourself schedule built on Serverless Jobs. Snapshots bill at €0.000049/GB/hour.

source.quote: Creating an image is free. However, the image feature creates snapshots of your volumes, and snapshots are billed separately.

files-survive-stop.note: When stopping you choose to keep local storage attached (billed as storage) or archive it to the volume store, from which it is restored on the next start. Block volumes are persistent independently of the Instance.

source.quote: Stopped (keep local storage): storage + IP (no compute).

volumes.note: Block volumes attach and detach like a virtual hard drive, up to 16 volumes per Instance including the boot volume, and 15 TB each. They persist without an Instance and are billed by provisioned size.

source.quote: Block volumes provide network-attached storage you can plug in/out of Instances like a virtual hard drive.

shared-volume.note: A block volume is attached to an Instance, and Scaleway documents no multi-attach mode that would let two Instances mount the same volume. Sharing files between machines means Object Storage, File Storage or a network service.

source.quote: Scaleway Block Storage volumes must be attached to an Instance before being used.

mount-buckets.shortfall: Object Storage speaks the S3 API, but Scaleway offers no native mount: you add s3fs, rclone or a similar client yourself, with the latency and consistency that implies.
mount-buckets.note: Object Storage is S3-compatible and priced separately (75 GB of egress free a month, then €0.01/GB). File Storage is a managed NFS-style file system, also a separate product.

source.quote: Scalable, fast and reliable Amazon S3-compatible storage platform for your data.

big-disk.note: A single block volume can be 15 TB, and up to 15 of them attach to one Instance. Local storage is capped at 600 GB on GP1-XL.

source.quote: The maximum size of a block volume is 15 TB.

stay-on.note: Nothing in the product stops a running Instance for idleness and there is no maximum session length. An always-on agent stays up until you stop or delete the machine.

source.quote: The Instance is fully active and consumes compute resources.

choose-idle.note: There is no idle timeout, auto-stop or sleep setting to configure. Stopping is a manual or API action, and standby mode bills in full.

source.quote: The Instance is halted and the underlying hypervisor is released.

wake-on-request.note: A stopped Instance has released its hypervisor and cannot be woken by an incoming request; something must call the API to start it. There is no request-triggered cold start.

source.quote: The Instance is halted and the underlying hypervisor is released.

schedules.note: Scaleway has no cron or scheduled start/stop for Instances. Autoscaling groups scale on metrics, not on a timetable; scheduling means cron or a systemd timer inside the machine, or Serverless Jobs calling the API.

source.quote: A group can run at a fixed size for predictable workloads, or scale automatically between a minimum and maximum number of Instances based on usage metrics.

public-url.note: A flexible IPv4 is routed directly to the Instance and any port can be opened through the security group; a free flexible IPv6 is also available. There is no provider-issued preview URL.

source.quote: Flexible routed IPv4 addresses: public IPv4 addresses routed directly to your Instance.

private-url.note: There is no private or token-gated URL for a port. Access control is the security group plus whatever authentication you run, or a private network with no public address.

source.quote: Detaching your Instance's flexible (public) IP address cuts any ongoing public connection to the Instance.

ssh.note: SSH is a normal daemon on a public address, with the key you uploaded at creation. There is no provider-only shell requirement.

source.quote: you can use a terminal application on your local computer to remotely connect to your Instance as root.

web-terminal.note: The console opens a serial TTY in a pop-up where you can run commands like an SSH shell, useful when the network is broken. You must set a Linux user password over SSH first.

source.quote: You can now run all Linux commands like in an SSH shell.

tunnel.note: Because SSH is a real port, local port forwarding works for reaching a dashboard or an agent UI without exposing it. No provider tunnel client is needed.

source.quote: you can use a terminal application on your local computer to remotely connect to your Instance as root.

raw-tcp.note: The security group filters inbound and outbound traffic by protocol and port, so non-web services, game servers and custom protocols work. SMTP is blocked by default until enabled.

source.quote: Define the inbound and outbound rules of the security group

custom-domain.note: A fixed public IP means an A or AAAA record is enough; Scaleway also sells Domains and DNS. There is no managed per-Instance hostname or domain mapping.

source.quote: public IPv4 addresses routed directly to your Instance.

auto-https.shortfall: Automatic HTTPS is not a property of an Instance: you either run Caddy or certbot on the server or put a paid Load Balancer (optionally with Edge Services) in front for a managed Let's Encrypt certificate.
auto-https.note: Edge Services terminates TLS with an uploaded certificate or a managed Let's Encrypt certificate, but only for an Object Storage bucket, a Load Balancer or a Serverless Container backend, not directly for an Instance.

source.quote: You can choose between uploading your own certificate held in Scaleway Secret Manager, or letting Edge Services generate a fully-managed Let's Encrypt certificate.

egress-included.note: Scaleway states that Instance list prices include egress and that there are no egress fees; the meter is the shape's public bandwidth, from 100 Mbps to 16 Gbps. Object Storage egress is a separate product.

source.quote: List prices include egress and IPv6 addresses.

egress-allowlist.note: Security groups are stateful or stateless firewalls with inbound and outbound rules, applied to the Instance's public traffic and to private-network interfaces.

source.quote: Define the inbound and outbound rules of the security group

no-internet.note: An Instance can be created without a flexible IPv4 and attached only to a Private Network, giving it no internet path at all.

source.quote: You can create an Instance without a flexible IPv4 by unticking the corresponding checkbox.

static-ip.note: A flexible IPv4 stays reserved to the account while the Instance is powered off and can be moved between Instances; it is billed until deleted. IPv6 is free.

source.quote: Billing for an Instance stops when it is powered off, but its flexible IPv4 remains reserved and continues to be billed unless deleted.

secrets-store.note: Secret Manager is a separate Scaleway product with versioned secrets, paths, ephemeral policies, single-access secrets and a time to live of up to a year. It is not wired into Instance creation; the agent reads it with an API key or you inject the value yourself.

source.quote: An ephemeral secret is a secret that has a limited lifetime, enforced by an ephemeral policy.

hidden-secrets.figure: No injection the agent can't read
hidden-secrets.note: Secrets are readable by any principal with the permission set that covers them. There is no write-only environment store or proxy that lets an agent use a key it cannot read, so a key on the machine is a key the agent can exfiltrate.

source.quote: Disabling a version is the action of temporarily revoking access to the data contained within a specific version.

scoped-keys.note: API keys belong to an IAM user or application and permissions come from policies with permission sets, resource scopes and CEL conditions, so a key can be limited to one project or one action.

source.quote: This allows fine-grained access to be defined for the IAM user bearing the API key across different Organizations, Projects, and resources.

dashboard-create.note: The console creates an Instance from an image or a template, with offer, zone, volumes, security group and cloud-init in one flow. It also shows an estimated cost before you confirm.

source.quote: You can create an Instance from scratch or from an Instance template.

cli.note: The official `scw` CLI covers Instances, volumes, snapshots, IPs and the rest of the platform, and is the same tool the docs use for scripted creation.

source.quote: This page shows the most common Scaleway CLI commands for creating and managing Scaleway Instances.

python-sdk.note: An official Python SDK is documented and published, in synchronous and asynchronous flavours. Scaleway labels it beta.

source.quote: The Scaleway Python SDK offers an efficient way for developers to interact with Scaleway's cloud services programmatically.

ts-sdk.note: An official JavaScript/TypeScript SDK is documented and published on npm as @scaleway/sdk, but it is designed for Node.js only: browser-based requests are not supported. Go is also supported.

source.quote: The Scaleway JS SDK is a dynamic tool for developers who use JavaScript to interact with Scaleway's cloud services.

rest-api.note: Every resource is available over the REST API with per-product OpenAPI specifications, and the API is what the console and CLI call.

source.quote: Manage your resources with the Scaleway API using simple HTTP requests.

mcp-server.note: Scaleway publishes no official MCP server for its control plane; the developer site lists API, SDKs, CLI and third-party integrations. Community servers such as scaleway-mcp exist but are third-party and were not evaluated.

source.quote: Manage your resources with the Scaleway API using simple HTTP requests.

pty.note: There is no API that opens an interactive shell in an Instance. Automation runs over SSH or cloud-init; the browser serial console is a human troubleshooting tool, not an API.

source.quote: You can now run all Linux commands like in an SSH shell.

file-api.note: Files move over SSH, SCP/SFTP or Object Storage. There is no per-Instance file read/write API.

source.quote: Manage your resources with the Scaleway API using simple HTTP requests.

agents-preinstalled.note: The InstantApps are infrastructure and web apps (Docker, GitLab, Nextcloud, WordPress, OpenVPN). No coding agent, no Hermes and no OpenClaw image.

source.quote: An InstantApp allows you to deploy pre-configured applications quickly on CPU Instances.

prompt-api.note: There is no prompt endpoint for an Instance. Scaleway's Generative APIs are a separate model service, not a way to prompt a machine.

source.quote: Manage your resources with the Scaleway API using simple HTTP requests.

one-click-hermes.note: Hermes is not in Scaleway's InstantApp list and Scaleway publishes no Hermes guide. You install it over SSH like any other service.

source.quote: An InstantApp allows you to deploy pre-configured applications quickly on CPU Instances.

one-click-openclaw.figure: Model API only, not an app
one-click-openclaw.note: Scaleway documents OpenClaw as a client of its Generative APIs on a local machine or Mac mini, not as an Instance image. Hosting the Gateway on an Instance is a manual install.

source.quote: You can integrate Openclaw with Generative APIs models to build a personal AI assistant

browser.note: No browser image or headless-browser service. You install Chromium or Playwright on the Instance, and memory is the constraint: 4 GiB is a practical floor for a browser agent.

source.quote: An InstantApp allows you to deploy pre-configured applications quickly on CPU Instances.

desktop.shortfall: There is a Windows Server image with Remote Desktop, but no managed desktop for computer-use agents; a Linux desktop means installing X, VNC or a remote-desktop stack yourself.
desktop.note: Scaleway's Windows golden-image guide enables Remote Desktop and the RDP firewall rule, so a Windows Instance gives a GUI over RDP. GPU remote-desktop images exist for Linux but are outside this card.

source.quote: Enables Remote Desktop

hosts-other-agents.shortfall: Scaleway documents OpenClaw only as a client of its model API on a local machine, and publishes no Instance guide for OpenClaw or Hermes; a third-party guide recommends DEV1-M.
hosts-other-agents.note: Any Linux VPS can host these agents, and a third-party deployment guide (DeployClaw) picks DEV1-M for OpenClaw. Scaleway's own content covers the model endpoint, not the Gateway host.

source.quote: You can integrate Openclaw with Generative APIs models to build a personal AI assistant

team-workspace.note: An Organization holds Projects and Members; resources live in a Project and access is granted per principal. A billing contact can be added separately.

source.quote: An Organization is made of one or several Projects.

roles.note: Predefined permission sets (InstancesFullAccess, InstancesReadOnly, BillingManager and dozens more) are attached to users, groups or applications through policies, with resource and CEL conditions.

source.quote: Permissions sets and their scope make up IAM rules, which define the access rights that a principal (user, group or application) should have.

sso.note: Identity Federation supports SAML single sign-on and SCIM user/group provisioning. The Organization Owner cannot use SAML and logs in with OAuth2; members must exist in the Organization first.

source.quote: Scaleway supports Identity Federation to provide your teams with secure access to their accounts via SAML Single Sign-On.

spend-cap.note: Billing alerts notify at a percentage of a monthly budget by SMS, email or webhook, but nothing blocks or stops a resource when the budget is reached. Quotas limit how many machines exist, not what they spend.

source.quote: This feature allows you to create alerts that notify you when predefined budget thresholds are met.

usage-alerts.note: Up to ten alerts per monthly budget, at chosen percentages, by SMS, email or API webhook, plus a consumption view by product. Alerts are based on the amount charged after tax and discounts.

source.quote: This feature allows you to create alerts that notify you when predefined budget thresholds are met.

audit-log.note: Audit Trail records successful, attempted and failed actions with the principal, API method, outcome and source IP, and can export the last 90 days to Object Storage daily.

source.quote: Audit Trail is a tool that holds a record of events and changes performed within a Scaleway Organization.

per-second.note: Each resource is billed for a minimum of 60 minutes per start and stop event, so a ten-minute run pays a full hour of compute. This is the single biggest difference from a sandbox provider.

source.quote: Each of these resources is billed separately for a minimum of 60 minutes.

active-cpu.note: CPU is allocated to the Instance for as long as it is powered on, and billed per hour of uptime whether the agent is busy or idle. Only powering off stops the compute meter.

source.quote: CPU Instances: Billed per hour of uptime (including startup and standby time).

cheap-pause.note: Powering off stops compute billing and keeps the disk; you still pay for attached storage and any reserved flexible IPv4. That is a genuine cheap idle state, unlike a VPS that bills while powered off.

source.quote: Compute billing stops, but you continue to pay for any attached storage (local volumes that you chose to keep or Block Storage volumes) and for any Flexible IPs.

no-monthly-fee.note: There is no subscription or plan fee: usage is invoiced monthly at the hourly rates, with no minimum commitment or notice period. Savings Plans are optional.

source.quote: You can power off or delete your Instance at any time—no minimum commitment or notice period is required.

flat-price.shortfall: There is no monthly price cap: the 'approx. per month' figure is simply the hourly rate multiplied by 730, so an always-on month costs exactly that and a partial month costs the hours used.
flat-price.note: Billing is by the hour of uptime, so the monthly figure is an estimate rather than a cap. A powered-off month costs only storage and IP.

source.quote: CPU Instances: Billed per hour of uptime (including startup and standby time).

free-tier.note: Scaleway has free tiers for some products, but no Instance size is free and the pricing page lists a price for every offer. The cheapest listed offer is STARDUST1-S at €0.0006/hour.

source.quote: Scaleway offers free tiers for certain products.

free-credit.note: New Business customers with a valid payment method and no previous Scaleway invoice get €100 of credit through a voucher emailed within 24 hours, which must be redeemed. It is a one-off trial, not a recurring allowance.

source.quote: Create a Business account and get started with €100 free credit.

no-card.note: A credit or debit card is required at signup, and must stay on the account even when SEPA is the payment method. Prepaid and virtual cards are refused.

source.quote: Note that you must add a credit card to your account before setting up a SEPA mandate.

status-page.note: A public status page lists incidents and scheduled maintenance per product and region, and the account docs describe subscribing to status updates.

source.quote: Scheduled maintenance is still in progress.

sla.shortfall: The cheap ranges have no service-level objective at all: DEV1, GP1, PLAY2 and PRO2 are listed as 'No SLO', and only BASIC3-X among the shared ranges carries 99%.
sla.note: Covered Shared Instances (BASIC2-A, BASIC3-X) get 99%, dedicated and specialized ranges 99.5%. Unavailability means at least four continuous minutes without external connectivity, and credits are a percentage of the monthly bill.

source.quote: No SLO

soc2.note: Scaleway advertises ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and HDS, with SecNumCloud under assessment. No SOC 2 report is listed on its security and compliance page; buyers who need SOC 2 must ask sales.

source.quote: Scaleway is committed to obtaining the most stringent certifications (ISO 27001, HDS, SecNumCloud – currently undergoing assessment)

dpa.note: A Data Processing Agreement is published alongside the General Terms and can be downloaded from the contracts page; the privacy policy states that processor data is governed by it.

source.quote: The data collected for the operation of our services, where Scaleway acts as a processor, is governed by our General Conditions of Services as well as our Data Processing Agreement (DPA).

open-source.note: The platform is proprietary. The CLI, SDKs and Terraform provider are open source, and Scaleway markets open standards and no vendor lock-in, but there is no self-hostable version of the cloud.

source.quote: Built on leading open-source technologies such as Kubernetes
